response.answer: IMPORTANT NOTE: The "Bataleon Goliath 2027" uses snowboard industry model-year naming conventions. The 2025/2026 season model is sold as "2026" by some retailers and the product asked about — listed as "2027" by the merchant — is the upcoming 2026/2027 season version. Specifications below are drawn from the manufacturer's most current listing and other authoritative sources. Note that this is the standard Goliath, NOT the Goliath+ (Plus), which is a distinct, higher-spec model. BRAND & COMPANY INFORMATION 1. Brand: Bataleon [1] 2. Model name: Goliath [1] 3. Model year (industry): 2027 (for 2026/2027 season) [2] 4. Product type: Snowboard [1] 5. Gender: Men's [3] 6. Manufacturer parent company: Bataleon is part of Low Pressure Studio, which was acquired by the Nidecker Group (NDK Group) in 2018 [4] 7. Brand founded: 2000 (some sources say late 1990s / 2001; there is a minor disagreement across sources) [5][6] — DISAGREEMENT: Onboard Mag and Boardertown say "2000" and "2001" respectively; Snowleader says "late 1990s". The most common reference is 2000. 8. Brand founder: Jørgen Karlsen (also spelled Karlson), a Norwegian biophysicist [5] 9. Brand headquarters: Amsterdam, Netherlands [7] 10. Board design location: Low Pressure Studio, Amsterdam [8] 11. Manufacturing location (current, per multiple sources): Austria — specifically at the CAPiTA Mothership factory [9] — DISAGREEMENT: SnowboardingProfiles reports manufacturing may have moved to Titan Factory in China or Saudi Arabia at some point; Whitelines and Powderforce say Austria/Mothership [10]. Most recent authoritative sources indicate Austria. 12. Manufacturing location (historical): Previously produced at Elan factory in Feistritz, Austria; temporarily moved to Asia after Elan closed [11] 13. Brand slogan: "Smile, It's Snowboarding" [12] 14. Warranty: 2+1 year warranty (2-year base + 1 additional year if product is registered) [3] 15. Return policy (Bataleon direct): 45-day returns [3] 16. Free shipping threshold (Bataleon US): Free shipping on orders over $50 [3] GOLIATH MODEL HISTORY & LEGACY 17. Model heritage: The Goliath is described as "the board that launched the 3D revolution" by Bataleon [3] 18. Goliath first available: Approximately 2004, per S2AS which describes it as "the most trusted ATV since '04" [13] 19. Board archive on Bataleon.com shows model years going back to at least 2004-05 season [14] 20. Model legacy: Selected for the Whitelines 100 Best Snowboard Gear Awards [15] 21. Model legacy: Described as Bataleon's "perennial bestseller" by Whitelines [16] 22. Customer review rating (Bataleon.com, 2025/26 model): 96% 5-star from 105 reviews [3] KEY SPECIFICATIONS (from manufacturer's own website, highest confidence) 23. Board category: All Mountain [2] 24. Shape: Directional Twin [3] 25. Camber type: Medium Camber with 3BT and SideKick [3] 26. Flex rating: 6/10 [3][13] 27. Nose sidebase uplift: Low [3] 28. Tail sidebase uplift: Low [3] 29. 3D shape: 3BT (Triple Base Technology) with SideKick [3] 30. Available sizes: 153cm, 156cm, 159cm, 158W, 161W, 164W, 167W [3] 31. Width options: Standard (153, 156, 159) and Wide (158W, 161W, 164W, 167W) [3] 32. Mounting pattern: 2x4 inserts [2] 33. Total inserts: 28 per board [3] 34. Insert material: A-grade German stainless steel [3] CORE MATERIAL — DISAGREEMENT NOTED 35. Core material (Bataleon.com 2025/26 Goliath page): Ultra Light Core — "A 70/30 Paulownia and poplar blend" [17] 36. Core material (merchant listing / The Source / Snowboard Shop): Ultra Light Core — "80/20 blend of Paulownia and poplar" [18] — DISAGREEMENT: The Bataleon.com own product page for the 2025/26 Goliath shows 70/30 while The Source and The Snowboard Shop list 80/20. The merchant listing says "1:2 blend of Poplar and Paulownia" which would be ~33/67. This is a three-way disagreement on the Paulownia-to-Poplar ratio. The most recent Bataleon.com page shows 70/30. 37. Core material (merchant listing from user): "Ultra Light Core (1:2 blend of Poplar and Paulownia)" [2] — Third variant of the ratio. CONSTRUCTION & MATERIALS 38. Fiberglass type: Tri-Ax (Tri-Axial) lamination — three-way fiberglass weave [3] 39. Carbon reinforcement: Carbon Stringers — strategically placed to fine-tune flex, response, and feel [3] 40. Carbon technology: D.R.S.T. SuperTubes — six hollow carbon cylinders running parallel to sidecut radius [3] 41. Sidewall construction: Flex Walls — Urethane Poured Sidewalls (not standard ABS) [3] 42. Sidewall benefit: Exceptional shock absorption, reducing chatter and vibration [3] 43. Base material: Ultra Glide S — premium 7000-grade sintered base (ISOSPORT 7000 P-Tex) [3] 44. Additional inserts — Backseat +4: Extra inserts 4cm behind bottom inserts for powder setup [3] 45. Additional inserts — Backseat +2: Extra inserts with 4cm offset on front pack and 2cm on rear pack [3] SIZE-SPECIFIC SPECIFICATIONS (from Bataleon.com) 46. Effective edge 153cm: 117.9cm [3] 47. Effective edge 156cm: 120.2cm [3] 48. Effective edge 159cm: 122.5cm [3] 49. Effective edge 158W: 121.7cm [3] 50. Effective edge 161W: 124.0cm [3] 51. Effective edge 164W: 126.3cm [3] 52. Effective edge 167W: 128.6cm [3] 53. Sidecut radius 153cm: 7.73m [3] 54. Sidecut radius 156cm: 7.85m [3] 55. Sidecut radius 159cm: 7.97m [3] 56. Sidecut radius 158W: 7.93m [3] 57. Sidecut radius 161W: 8.05m [3] 58. Sidecut radius 164W: 8.17m [3] 59. Sidecut radius 167W: 8.29m [3] 60. Waist width 153cm: 25.2cm [3] 61. Waist width 156cm: 25.4cm [3] 62. Waist width 159cm: 25.6cm [3] 63. Waist width 158W: 26.6cm [3] 64. Waist width 161W: 26.8cm [3] 65. Waist width 164W: 27.0cm [3] 66. Waist width 167W: 27.2cm [3] 67. Tip/Tail width 153cm: 29.4/29.4cm [3] 68. Tip/Tail width 156cm: 29.7/29.7cm [3] 69. Tip/Tail width 159cm: 30.9/30.9cm [3] 70. Tip/Tail width 158W: 30.1/30.1cm [3] 71. Tip/Tail width 161W: 31.3/31.3cm [3] 72. Tip/Tail width 164W: 31.6/31.6cm [3] 73. Tip/Tail width 167W: 31.9/31.9cm [3] 74. Min/Max stance 153cm: 49.0-61.0cm [3] 75. Min/Max stance 156cm: 51.0-63.0cm [3] 76. Min/Max stance 159cm: 52.0-64.0cm [3] 77. Min/Max stance 158W: 51.0-63.0cm [3] 78. Min/Max stance 161W: 52.0-64.0cm [3] 79. Min/Max stance 164W: 53.0-65.0cm [3] 80. Min/Max stance 167W: 54.0-65.0cm [3] 81. Recommended weight 153cm: 61-81kg (134-178 lbs) [3] 82. Recommended weight 156cm: 67-87kg (147-191 lbs) [3] 83. Recommended weight 159cm: 75-95kg (165-209 lbs) [3] 84. Recommended weight 158W: 73-93kg (161-205 lbs) [3] 85. Recommended weight 161W: 79-99kg (174-218 lbs) [3] 86. Recommended weight 164W: 85-105kg (187-231 lbs) [3] 87. Recommended weight 167W: 103-123kg (227-271 lbs) [3] 88. Wide board recommended boot size: UK 10.5 or larger [19] 89. Boot size range (standard 153-159): EU 39-44, US 7-10 [3] 90. Boot size range (wide 158W-167W): EU 42-48, US 9-14 [3] TERRAIN & RIDING STYLE 91. Terrain: Powder, Park, Groomers [2] 92. Riding style: All-mountain freestyle — blends freestyle agility with freeride power [3] 93. Target rider: Intermediate to advanced riders looking for one-board quiver [13] 94. Target rider (Whitelines): Progressing snowboarders who want a board for all conditions [16] 95. Ability level (merchant listing): Intermediate [2] 96. Ability level (SnowboardingProfiles): Fine for low intermediate riders; high-end beginners may be OK with it [20] 97. Use case: One-board quiver / "quiver killer" [13] 98. Switch riding capability: Rides switch very well due to near-twin design — "rides switch perfectly" per reviewer [21] PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS (from independent reviews) 99. Pop: Exceptional — "The pop is unreal" and "ollies incredibly well" per The Good Ride [22] 100. Edge catch resistance: Very catch-free — "super catch-free" per SnowboardingProfiles [20] 101. Turn initiation: Very easy to initiate turns [20] 102. Maneuverability at low speed: Quick edge-to-edge at slower speeds [20] 103. Carving capability: Good but not epic — "a pretty good board to carve on, not an epic carver" per SnowboardingProfiles [20] 104. Carving feel with 3BT: Edge engagement point is lower/deeper in the carving motion than traditional boards [20] 105. Carving speed suitability: Good for moderate and slower speed carves; less suitable for high-speed carves [23] 106. High speed stability (negative): "Gets a bit wobbly when opening it out to moderately fast speeds" per SnowboardingProfiles [20] 107. Crud/chunder performance (negative): "Gets bucked around pretty easily and is a little chattery in crud/chunder" per SnowboardingProfiles [20] 108. Edge hold on hard/icy snow (negative): "edgeless washy feel in medium to hard snow" per The Good Ride [24] 109. Edge hold concern: "really had trouble holding an edge in hard snow and it was really sketchy" per The Good Ride [24] 110. Buttering: Very good — flat sections in nose/tail aid buttering [24] 111. Powder float: Good for an all-mountain board; TBT helps float despite camber [22] 112. Weight feel: Lighter on the scales vs average and even lighter feeling when riding per SnowboardingProfiles [20] 113. Weight assessment from The Good Ride: "on the lighter side of normal" [24] 114. Overall reviewer impression (SnowboardingProfiles): "a great all-rounder, capable of almost anything" [20] 115. Overall impression (Whitelines): "a true all-mountain legend" [16] 116. Overall impression (Wobble Snow): "like slipping into a comfy pair of slippers" [25] USER REVIEW THEMES 117. Positive user review: "It was instantly easier to control than my old board. My confidence increased exponentially." (Bataleon.com review) [3] 118. Positive user review: "Feels super light under foot. Super easy to turn and stable enough for my riding style." (Bataleon.com review) [3] 119. Positive user review: "Super good feedback and stable to really go flat out and a good allrounder to have some fun in the park" (Bataleon.com review) [26] 120. Negative user review: Customer service issues reported — "Customer service was unhelpful, and the email communication was poorly written" (Bataleon.com review) [3] 121. Negative user review: Shipping was "extremely delayed" for one customer [3] 122. 3BT learning curve: Some riders find 3BT takes getting used to — "takes a few days to understand" per The Good Ride [24] 123. 3BT feel: "they feel a bit different but I was instantly comfortable" per forum user [27] PRICING & AVAILABILITY 124. Price — Bataleon US (official, current/25-26 model, on sale): $440.95 (regular $629.95, 30% off) [3] 125. Price — Bataleon US MSRP: $629.95 [3] 126. Price — evo.com (2026 model on sale): $440.96 (from $629.95) [28] 127. Price — Whitelines reference (2024-25 model): $629 at evo.com [16] 128. Price — S2AS (2027 Goliath, USD): $623.00 [29] — Note: this is the 2027 model, pre-order 129. Price — S2AS (2027 Goliath+, USD): $673.00 [30] — Note: this is the Plus variant 130. Price — Merchant listing (AUD): $1,079.99 [2] 131. Availability status (merchant): Preorder, estimated May 1, 2026 [2] 132. Availability (Bataleon US 2025/26 model): All sizes sold out [3] 133. Availability (Balmoral Boards, Australia): Pre-order, expected delivery April/May 2026 [31] 134. Availability (S2AS, 2027 model): Pre-order/low stock [29] 135. Availability (The Snowboard Shop UK, 2027 Goliath+): Backordered, pre-order [19] 136. Shipping restriction (merchant): Only available for shipping within Australia [2] RETAILERS & THEIR REPUTATION 137. Retailer: Bataleon.com (official) — direct-to-consumer, 45-day returns, 2+1 year warranty, free shipping >$50 [3] 138. Retailer: evo.com — major US online retailer, price match policy ("We'll beat it by 5%"), up to 1 year returns, free shipping, membership rewards [28] 139. Retailer: Surface 2 Air Sports (S2AS) — UK-based authorised Bataleon retailer, 15+ years selling Bataleon, price match guarantee, ships internationally [29] 140. Retailer: The Source Snowboard & Skate — North American speciality shop [32] 141. Retailer: Blauer Board Shop — US-based speciality snowboard shop [33] 142. Retailer: The Snowboard Shop (UK) — UK speciality retailer, Klarna/Clearpay payment options [19] 143. Retailer: Balmoral Boards (Australia) — Australian speciality shop, $10 flat rate shipping Australia-wide, lay-by available [31] 144. Retailer: Absolute Snow (UK) — UK retailer stocking Bataleon [34] 145. Retailer tip (forum): "Buy your board from Canada. Shipping to America is typically $30" with favorable currency exchange [27] RELATED MODELS & VARIANTS 146. Higher-spec variant: Bataleon Goliath+ (Plus) — stiffer flex (7/10), Super Ultra Light Core with AirRide Technology, Aramid X-Ply, Nano Speed sintered base; designed for intermediate-to-advanced riders wanting more power [35] 147. Goliath vs Goliath+ flex difference: Goliath is 6/10; Goliath+ is 7/10 [13][35] 148. Goliath vs Goliath+ core difference: Goliath uses Ultra Light Core; Goliath+ uses Super Ultra Light Core (80/20 Paulownia/Poplar) with AirRide [18][35] 149. Goliath vs Goliath+ pop difference: Goliath+ has more pop per The Good Ride [22] 150. Goliath vs Goliath+ dampening: Goliath+ has AirRide vibration dampening; standard Goliath does not [35] 151. Lower-level alternative within Bataleon: Bataleon Whatever — softer flex (5/10), similar shape [36] 152. Even lower alternative: Bataleon Fun.Kink — medium-soft flex (4/10) [37] COMPETITOR COMPARISONS 153. Key competitor: Jones Mountain Twin — better edge hold on ice/hard snow than Goliath per SnowboardingProfiles [38] 154. Key competitor: YES Standard — frequently compared as a top all-mountain one-board quiver [39] 155. Key competitor: Capita Mercury / Mega Merc — more aggressive edge-to-edge per Board of the World [40] 156. Competitor list from SnowboardingProfiles review comments: Jones Frontier, Jones Mountain Twin, YES Standard, GNU 4x4, Arbor Shiloh Camber [38] 157. Competitor list from The Good Ride: Korua Otto, Ride Algorythm, Salomon Highpath, YES Standard Uninc, Capita Black Snowboard of Death, Jones Rally Cat, Nitro Alternator [22] 158. Bataleon Goliath vs Jones Mountain Twin (forum): "The mountain twin with edge tech and less 3D shaping maybe has a touch more edge hold but doesn't feel as aggressive as the Goliath because of the camber profile" [27] 159. Competitor edge hold advantage: Jones Mountain Twin has magnetraction-like edge tech; Goliath does not [38] 160. Goliath advantage over competitors: More catch-free and forgiving than traditional cambered all-mountain boards [27] 3BT TECHNOLOGY DETAILS 161. 3BT definition: Triple Base Technology — 3D base shaping with lifted sidebases, flat center base, positive camber from nose to tail [3] 162. 3BT benefit: Reduces risk of edge catch while maintaining ollie power and carving control [2] 163. SideKick definition: Increases sidebase uplift beyond widest points of nose and tail, giving tips a hull-like shape [3] 164. SideKick benefit: Enhanced float in deep snow and smoother turn initiation [3] 165. D.R.S.T. SuperTubes: Six hollow carbon cylinders running along sidecut radius — increase power transfer to edges, enhance camber, reduce weight, increase pop [3] 166. 3BT is unique to Bataleon (patented): "Triple Base Technology is patented" [41] 167. 3BT Goliath variant: Low 3BT for Bataleon's scale, but more lifted than competitors' 3D shaping [24] BINDING COMPATIBILITY & SETUP 168. Binding compatibility: Standard 2x4 insert pattern — compatible with majority of snowboard bindings (non-Burton EST) [19] 169. Binding recommendation (user): Union Force bindings with full-size discs work well; Bataleon's own Astro/Atom have small discs limiting setback adjustment [22] 170. Recommended Bataleon binding: Astro Fullwrap [42] ADDITIONAL FACTS 171. Weight recommendation accuracy: "Bataleon is pretty spot on with recommended weight but very liberal with recommended boot sizing" per The Good Ride [22] 172. Directional twin detail: "slightly longer nose than tail but everything else is pretty symmetrical" — nose is approximately 1cm longer [43] 173. Shape description: "Rides almost like a true twin with a centered feel underfoot" on groomers [24] 174. Setback on 156cm Goliath: 2.875" back from center using full-size disc bindings [22] 175. Annual model changes: The Goliath appears to have minimal spec changes year-to-year — "doesn't seem to be changing for 2026" per The Good Ride (written late 2025) [24]
